committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts new and existing employees of the DHS Office of Intelligence and Analysis, as well as GAO oversight staff.
dimensions.evidence: implement a standardized entry-level basic intelligence training curricula for all employees of the Office of Intelligence and Analysis

dimensions.assessment: Modifies internal training protocols, adding mandatory privacy, civil rights, analytic, and open-source collection curricula for personnel.
dimensions.evidence: include training on civil rights, civil liberties, privacy rights, regulations, and information practices

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state explicit dollar amounts or appropriations for implementing the training programs.
Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to mandate new internal agency training structures, tracking systems, and regular reports.
dimensions.evidence: Section 201 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 121) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes ongoing annual reporting requirements for five years and permanent standardized entry-level training rules for future hires.
dimensions.evidence: annually thereafter for five years, the Under Secretary for Intelligence and Analysis shall submit

missing_information: Cost estimates or authorized funding levels for developing and tracking the training programs.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill standardizes and formalizes training programs for new employees within the Department of Homeland Security's Office of Intelligence and Analysis, establishing tracking systems and congressional reporting requirements.
